name: Local GPU
summary: Run open-weight models on hardware you own, such as a workstation GPU, an Apple Silicon Mac or an on-prem server, and point the agent at a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. There is no per-token bill and prompts never leave the machine, but model size and speed are capped by your memory and compute.
how: Pick an open-weight model that fits your GPU or unified memory, usually a quantized build
Serve it with a local runtime such as Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or vLLM
Point the agent at the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Keep a hosted model as a fallback for tasks the local model can't handle
facts: Hardware and power up front, no per-token fees
Prompts and data stay on your machine
Smaller models and lower throughput than hosted frontier APIs
goodFor: High-volume background tasks with no token bill
watchOut: Large models need a lot of VRAM or unified memory
Quantized small models are weaker at long agentic tool use
You maintain drivers, runtimes and updates
